entries.englishValue: Bitcoin doesn't have inflation
entries.targetTranslation: Bitcoin ilibe kukwera kwa mitengo

entries.englishValue: Inflation means your money buys you less over time. Bitcoin is better money because it doesn't have inflation.
entries.targetTranslation: Kukwera kwa mitengo kumatanthauza kuti ndalama zanu zimakhoza kugula zochepa pakapita nthawi. Bitcoin ndi ndalama yabwino chifukwa ilibe kukwera kwa mitengo.

entries.englishValue: because it has a maximum supply of 21 million Bitcoin. No one can print more Bitcoin.
entries.targetTranslation: , chifukwa kuchuluka kwake kwakukulu ndi 21 miliyoni ya Bitcoin. Palibe amene angasindikize Bitcoin yowonjezeka.

entries.englishValue: Dollars have an unlimited supply, which means more can be printed at any time.
entries.targetTranslation: Dola ya Australia ili ndi kuchuluka kopanda malire, zomwe zikutanthauza kuti pamakhalapo zambiri zomwe zingasindikizidwe.

entries.englishValue: Bitcoin is scarce
entries.targetTranslation: Bitcoin ndi yochepa

entries.englishValue: Historically, Bitcoin has gained purchasing power over time while the dollar has lost it. Many people use Bitcoin as their long-term savings account: money that they can leave alone and let grow for several years.
entries.targetTranslation: M'mbuyomu, Bitcoin yawonjezera mphamvu zogula pakapita nthawi, pomwe dola ya australia ikutaya mphamvu yake yogula. Anthu ambiri amagwiritsa ntchito Bitcoin ngati akaunti yosungira kwa nthawi yayitali — ndalama zomwe amasunga zaka zambiri popanda kuzigwira pomwe mtengo wake ukukwera.

entries.englishValue: Would you rather save in dollars that buy you less over time? Or save in Bitcoin that has historically bought you more over time?
entries.targetTranslation: Ndi chiyani chomwe mungafune kwambiri: kusunga mu madola a Australia — madola a Australia omwe akhoza kugula zochepa pakapita nthawi — kapena kusunga mu Bitcoin, yomwe m'mbuyomu yakhoza kugula zochuluka pakapita nthawi?

entries.englishValue: Bitcoin is also a tool for freedom
entries.targetTranslation: Bitcoin ndi chida cha ufulu

entries.englishValue: The Bitcoin network isn't owned by anyone. It isn't controlled by any government or corporation. It's designed to uphold your freedom and protect your money.
entries.targetTranslation: Netiweki ya Bitcoin sili ya munthu aliyense. Palibe boma kapena kampani yomwe imayilamulira. Idamangidwa kuti iteteze ufulu wanu ndi ndalama zanu.

entries.englishValue: People around the world are already using Bitcoin to protect their freedom — even when their own governments refused to help or tried to stop them.
entries.targetTranslation: Lero, anthu padziko lonse akugwiritsa ntchito Bitcoin kuti ateteze ufulu wawo — ngakhale pamene maboma awo akukana kuwathandiza kapena kuyesa kuwaletsa.

entries.englishValue: If you save in Australian Dollars, you've probably noticed that they buy you less each year. It takes more dollars to buy the same amount of food. You need more dollars to maintain your quality of life.
entries.targetTranslation: Ngati mukusunga mu madola a Australia, mwina mwazindikira kuti ndalama zanu zikhoza kugula zochepa. Mukufunika madola a Australia yochuluka kuti mugule zinthu zomwezo. Mukufunika madola a Australia yochuluka kuti mukhalebe ndi moyo wamtundu womwewo.

entries.englishValue: But it doesn't have to be this way.
entries.targetTranslation: Koma sizifunika kukhala chonchi.

entries.englishValue: People who saved in Bitcoin over the last 4 years saw life get cheaper.
entries.targetTranslation: Moyo wakhala wotsika mtengo kwa anthu omwe akhala akusunga mu Bitcoin pa zaka 4 zapitazi.

entries.englishValue: Here's the proof: your money is losing value
entries.targetTranslation: Apa pali umboni: ndalama zanu zikupitirizabe kutaya mtengo wake

entries.englishValue: The dollars in your bank account buy you less every year. That's because there is no fixed limit on how many dollars can be created.
entries.targetTranslation: dola ya Australia iliyonse yomwe mumasunga m'banki imataya mtengo wake chaka ndi chaka. Izi zikuchitika chifukwa palibe malire a kuchuluka kwa madola a Australia omwe angapangidwe.

entries.englishValue: This unlimited supply is the root cause of inflation. Over recent years, the total amount of dollars in existence has increased dramatically.
entries.targetTranslation: Kuchuluka kopanda malire ndiye chomwe chimayambitsa kukwera kwa mitengo. M'zaka zaposachedwa, kuchuluka kwa madola a Australia omwe akugwiritsidwa ntchito kwawonjezeka kwambiri.

entries.englishValue: When more money is created from nothing, the price of everything goes up. This includes the raw materials that companies buy to make their products — which means higher prices for you.
entries.targetTranslation: Ndalama zambiri zikamapangidwa kuchokera ku zopanda kanthu, zinthu zonse zimakwera mtengo. Kuphatikizapo zinthu zopangira zomwe makampani amagula popanga zinthu — zomwe zikutanthauza mitengo yokwera kwa inu.

entries.targetTranslation: Ngongole ya boma ikamawonjezeka, amasindikiza ndalama zambiri chifukwa anthu ochepa amafuna kukongoza ndalama ku boma.

entries.englishValue: Historically, Bitcoin has gained purchasing power over time while the yen has lost it. Many people use Bitcoin as their long-term savings account: money that they can leave alone and let grow for several years.
entries.targetTranslation: M'mbuyomu, Bitcoin yawonjezera mphamvu zogula pakapita nthawi, pomwe yen ya japan ikutaya mphamvu yake yogula. Anthu ambiri amagwiritsa ntchito Bitcoin ngati akaunti yosungira kwa nthawi yayitali — ndalama zomwe amasunga zaka zambiri popanda kuzigwira pomwe mtengo wake ukukwera.

entries.englishValue: Would you rather save in yen that buy you less over time? Or save in Bitcoin that has historically bought you more over time?
entries.targetTranslation: Ndi chiyani chomwe mungafune kwambiri: kusunga mu ma yen a Japan — ma yen a Japan omwe akhoza kugula zochepa pakapita nthawi — kapena kusunga mu Bitcoin, yomwe m'mbuyomu yakhoza kugula zochuluka pakapita nthawi?

entries.englishValue: Bitcoin is also a tool for freedom
entries.targetTranslation: Bitcoin ndi chida cha ufulu

entries.englishValue: The Bitcoin network isn't owned by anyone. It isn't controlled by any government or corporation. It's designed to uphold your freedom and protect your money.
entries.targetTranslation: Netiweki ya Bitcoin sili ya munthu aliyense. Palibe boma kapena kampani yomwe imayilamulira. Idamangidwa kuti iteteze ufulu wanu ndi ndalama zanu.

entries.englishValue: People around the world are already using Bitcoin to protect their freedom — even when their own governments refused to help or tried to stop them.
entries.targetTranslation: Lero, anthu padziko lonse akugwiritsa ntchito Bitcoin kuti ateteze ufulu wawo — ngakhale pamene maboma awo akukana kuwathandiza kapena kuyesa kuwaletsa.

entries.englishValue: If you save in Japanese Yen, you've probably noticed that they buy you less each year. It takes more yen to buy the same amount of food. You need more yen to maintain your quality of life.

entries.targetTranslation: Moyo wakhala wotsika mtengo kwa anthu omwe akhala akusunga mu Bitcoin pa zaka 4 zapitazi.

entries.englishValueBefore: Bitcoin prevents you from spending money you don't have - you can only spend Bitcoin that you actually own. Banks allow overdrafts (spending more than your account balance) and then charge substantial fees for this 'service,' often leading to cascading penalty charges.

entries.englishValueBefore: Bitcoin transactions are censorship resistant - once broadcast to the network, they cannot be stopped or reversed by any central authority. entries.englishValue: Once broadcast, Bitcoin transactions can't be stopped or reversed. Banks can block, freeze, or reverse transactions based on policy or government orders.

entries.englishValueBefore: Bitcoin operates independently of any government and cannot be controlled, inflated, or defaulted on by political authorities.
entries.englishValue: Bitcoin operates independently of any government or political authority.
entries.currentValue: Bitcoin imagwira ntchito modziyimira popanda boma lililonse ndipo singalamulire, kukweza, kapena kulephera ndi olamulira andale.
entries.targetTranslation: Bitcoin imagwira ntchito mwapayekha popanda boma kapena ulamuliro wandale.

entries.englishValueBefore: Bitcoin can be sent anywhere in the world instantly over the Internet, while cash requires physical presence or trusted intermediaries. You can't email cash, but you can send Bitcoin to anyone with an Internet connection in minutes.
entries.englishValue: Bitcoin moves over the internet anywhere in minutes. Cash needs physical presence or trusted couriers — you can't email a $20 bill.
entries.currentValue: Bitcoin imatha kutumizidwa kulikonse padziko lonse pa intaneti, pomwe ndalama zimafuna kukhalapo pamanjanja kapena kukhulupirira anthu apakati.
entries.targetTranslation: Bitcoin imayenda pa internet kulikonse mu mphindi zochepa. Ndalama zenizeni zimafunika kupezeka pamalo kapena otumiza odalirika — simungatumize ndalama zenizeni za $20 kudzera mu imelo.

entries.englishValueBefore: Bitcoin works the same way everywhere in the world - there are no borders in the Bitcoin network. Cash is limited by geography, exchange rates, and local acceptance. Try using US dollars in rural Thailand or Japanese yen in rural Mexico.
entries.englishValue: Bitcoin works the same way everywhere. Cash is limited by geography, exchange rates, and local acceptance.

entries.targetTranslation: Bitcoin imagwira ntchito chimodzimodzi kulikonse. Ndalama zenizeni zili zochepa pamalo, mtengo wa kusinthana, ndi kuvomerezeka kwa kumudzi.

entries.englishValueBefore: Bitcoin cannot be invalidated by any government or authority - it exists on a global, decentralized network that no single entity controls.

entries.targetTranslation: Bitcoin singathetsedwe ndi boma lililonse kapena ulamuliro uliwonse.

entries.englishValueBefore: Cash can be counterfeited, and it's often difficult to detect fake bills without special equipment. Even with security features, counterfeit cash continues to circulate. Bitcoin uses cryptographic proof that makes counterfeiting mathematically impossible.
entries.englishValue: Cash can be counterfeited, sometimes convincingly. Bitcoin uses cryptography that makes counterfeiting mathematically impossible.
entries.currentValue: Ndalama zimatha kupangidwa zachinyengo, ndipo nthawi zambiri n'kovuta kuzindikira ma noti achinyengo popanda zipangizo zapadera. Bitcoin imagwiritsa ntchito umboni wa cryptographic womwe umapangitsa kuti kuchinyengo kukhale kosatheka.
entries.targetTranslation: Ndalama zenizeni zikhoza kupangidwa zabodza, nthawi zina mwaluso. Bitcoin imagwiritsa ntchito cryptography yomwe imapangitsa kupanga zabodza kosatheka.

entries.englishValueBefore: Cash is issued and controlled by governments, who can print more at will, change designs, or declare certain bills invalid. Bitcoin operates on a decentralized network where no single authority has control over the money supply or rules.
entries.englishValue: Bitcoin has no central authority. Cash is issued by governments that can print more, change designs, or invalidate notes at will.
entries.currentValue: Ndalama zimatulutsdwa ndi kulamulira ndi maboma, omwe amatha kusindikiza zambiri, kusintha mapangidwe, kapena kunena kuti ma noti ena alibe ntchito. Bitcoin imagwira ntchito pa netiweki yogawidwa pomwe palibe olamulira mmodzi amene ali ndi ulamuliro.

entries.currentValue: Ndalama zili ndi malire ang'onoang'ono - simungathe kugawa senti kukhala zigawo zing'onozing'ono. Bitcoin imatha kugawidwa kukhala zigawo 100 miliyoni zomwe zimatchedwa satoshis, zomwe zimalola malipiro ang'onoang'ono ndi machitidwe olondola a ndalama zilizonse.

entries.englishValueBefore: Bitcoin is the most secure computing network that has ever existed and has never been hacked. CBDCs rely on governments and banks to secure the network, which have been hacked countless times throughout history.
entries.englishValue: Bitcoin is the most secure computing network ever built and has never been hacked. CBDCs rely on banks and governments that have been hacked countless times.

entries.englishValue: Bitcoin's rules are validated by tens of thousands of independent nodes. CBDCs are centralized in government and central-bank hands, which hold complete control over the network.

entries.englishValue: Anyone can run a Bitcoin node to verify the rules of the network. CBDCs don't allow users to run nodes — you have to trust the central authority.

entries.englishValueBefore: Bitcoin operates on a truly decentralized network with tens of thousands of independent nodes worldwide. Many crypto projects are controlled by foundations, companies, or small groups of developers who can make unilateral decisions about the protocol's future.
entries.englishValue: Bitcoin runs on tens of thousands of independent nodes worldwide. Most crypto projects are controlled by foundations, companies, or small dev teams that can make unilateral changes.

entries.englishValue: Bitcoin has one purpose: peer-to-peer digital money. Anyone can understand and use it. Most crypto involves complex smart contracts or DeFi that require technical expertise to use safely.
entries.currentValue: Bitcoin ili ndi cholinga chimodzi chosavuta: ndalama zadigitala zapakati pa anthu. Aliyense angamvetsetse ndi kuigwiritsa ntchito ndi chidziwitso choyambirira. Ntchito zambiri za crypto zimafuna chidziwitso chakuya cha teknoloji.
entries.targetTranslation: Bitcoin ili ndi cholinga chimodzi: ndalama za digito za peer-to-peer. Aliyense akhoza kuyimvetsa ndi kuyigwiritsa ntchito. Crypto yambiri imaphatikizapo zopangidwa zophweka kapena DeFi yomwe imafuna luso lapadera kuti igwiritsidwe ntchito motetezeka.

entries.englishValueBefore: Bitcoin uses Proof of Work consensus, which has been battle-tested for over 15 years without a single successful attack on the main network. Many crypto projects use experimental consensus mechanisms like Proof of Stake or delegated systems that haven't proven their long-term security.
entries.englishValue: Bitcoin's Proof of Work has run without a successful attack on the main network for over 15 years. Most crypto projects use experimental consensus that hasn't been battle-tested.
entries.currentValue: Bitcoin imagwiritsa ntchito Proof of Work yomwe yayesedwa kwa zaka zopitirira 15 popanda kupambana kwa chitukuko. Ntchito zambiri za crypto zimagwiritsa ntchito njira zoyesedwa monga Proof of Stake.
entries.targetTranslation: Proof of Work ya Bitcoin yakhala ikugwira ntchito popanda kuukira kopambana pa netiweki yaikulu kwa zaka 15 zoposa. Ma project ambiri a crypto amagwiritsa ntchito makonsensasi atsopano osayesedwa pamunda.

entries.englishValueBefore: Bitcoin serves as digital money - a store of value and medium of exchange. Most crypto tokens are utility tokens for specific platforms, governance tokens, or speculative assets with unclear real-world value propositions.
entries.englishValue: Bitcoin is digital money — a store of value and medium of exchange. Most crypto tokens are speculative utility or governance tokens with unclear real-world value.
entries.currentValue: Bitcoin imagwira ntchito ngati ndalama zadigitala - malo osungira chuma ndi njira yosinthiranira. Ma token ambiri a crypto ndi a ntchito za mapulatifomu apadera.
entries.targetTranslation: Bitcoin ndi ndalama za digito — malo osungira phindu ndi njira yosinthana. Ma token ambiri a crypto ndi ma token oyendetsa kapena olamulira osakaza ndi mtengo wokayikitsa wa dziko lenileni.

entries.englishValueBefore: Bitcoin becomes stronger under attack and has survived every crisis, ban, and criticism thrown at it. Most crypto projects are fragile and can collapse from regulatory pressure, technical failures, or market downturns.
entries.englishValue: Bitcoin grows stronger under attack and has survived every crisis, ban, and criticism. Most crypto projects collapse under regulatory, technical, or market pressure.
entries.currentValue: Bitcoin imalimba mukaukiwa ndipo yapulumuka kwa mavuto onse. Ntchito zambiri za crypto ndi zofooka ndipo zimatha kugwa chifukwa cha malamulo, mavuto ateknikaili, kapena kugwa kwa msika.
entries.targetTranslation: Bitcoin imakula yamphamvu pansi pa kuukira ndipo yapulumuka pa zovuta zonse, zoletsa, ndi kunyoza. Ma project ambiri a crypto amagwa pansi pa zovuta za malamulo, zaukadaulo, kapena za msika.

entries.englishValueBefore: Bitcoin has no CEO, no company behind it, and no single point of failure. Many crypto projects are backed by venture capital firms, have identifiable leadership teams, or depend on specific companies for their continued operation.
entries.englishValue: Bitcoin has no CEO, no company, no single point of failure. Most crypto projects depend on VCs, specific leadership, or one company's survival.
entries.currentValue: Bitcoin ilibe CEO, ilibe kampani yomwe ikuyichirikiza, ndipo ilibe malo ovutikira amodzi. Ntchito zambiri za crypto zimachirikizidwa ndi makampani a venture capital kapena zidalira makampani enieni.
entries.targetTranslation: Bitcoin ilibe CEO, ilibe kampani, ilibe malo amodzi olephera. Ma project ambiri a crypto amadalira ma VC, atsogoleri ena, kapena kupulumuka kwa kampani imodzi.

entries.englishValueBefore: Bitcoin is perfectly fungible, meaning every bitcoin is identical and interchangeable - one bitcoin equals one bitcoin anywhere in the world. Fine art is non-fungible by nature, with each piece being unique in its creation, history, condition, and provenance, making direct comparisons and valuations extremely difficult.
entries.englishValue: Every bitcoin is identical and interchangeable. Every artwork is unique — different creation, history, condition, and provenance make direct comparisons extremely difficult.
entries.currentValue: Bitcoin imagwira ntchito mofanana - bitcoin imodzi ndi yofanana ndi bitcoin ina iliyonse padziko lonse. Zojambula zapamwamba ndi zapadera pamapangidwe, mbiri, kuyendera, ndi chiyambi, zomwe zimapangitsa kuyerekezera ndi kuwerengera kukhala kovuta kwambiri.
entries.targetTranslation: Bitcoin iliyonse imafanana ndipo ingasinthidwe. Chojambula chilichonse ndi chapadera — kupangidwa kosiyana, mbiri, mkhalidwe, ndi chiyambi zimapangitsa kuyerekeza kwachindunji kukhala kovuta kwambiri.

entries.englishValueBefore: Bitcoin trades on a global 24/7 market where anyone with internet access can buy or sell instantly. Fine art requires specialized auction houses like Sotheby's or Christie's, private dealers, or exclusive galleries. Sales can take months to arrange and complete, with limited market access and irregular trading opportunities.
entries.englishValue: Bitcoin trades 24/7 on a global market accessible to anyone. Fine art requires specialized auction houses, private dealers, or galleries and can take months to sell.
entries.currentValue: Bitcoin imagulitsidwa pa msika wa 24/7 padziko lonse pomwe aliyense wokhala ndi intaneti amatha kugula kapena kugulitsa nthawi yomweyo. Zojambula zapamwamba zimafuna nyumba za malonda zapadera, ndipo malonda amatha kutenga miyezi.
entries.targetTranslation: Bitcoin imagulitsidwa 24/7 pa msika wa padziko lonse womwe ungafikidwe ndi aliyense. Zojambula zapamwamba zimafunika nyumba zapadera za auction, ogulitsa achinsinsi, kapena ma gallery ndipo zikhoza kutenga miyezi kuti zigulitsidwe.

entries.englishValueBefore: Buying or selling bitcoin typically costs less than 1% in fees, often much less. Fine art sales involve substantial costs including buyer's premiums (10-25%), seller's commissions (10-15%), insurance, transportation, storage, and authentication fees. These combined costs can easily exceed 30-40% of the artwork's value in a single transaction.
entries.englishValue: Buying or selling Bitcoin costs under 1% in fees, often much less. Art sales rack up 30–40% in buyer's premiums, commissions, insurance, transport, and authentication fees.
entries.currentValue: Kugula kapena kugulitsa bitcoin nthawi zambiri kumalandira malipiro ochepa kwambiri. Zojambula zapamwamba zimabweretsa ndalama zambirimbiri kuphatikiza malipiro oogula, malipiro a ogulitsa, inshulansi, kuyendetsa, ndi ena.
entries.targetTranslation: Kugula kapena kugulitsa Bitcoin kumawononga ndalama zochepera 1%, nthawi zambiri zochepa kwambiri. Kugulitsa kojambula kumawonjezera 30–40% mu premium ya wogula, ndalama, inshuwalansi, kunyamula, ndi ndalama zotsimikiziridwa.

entries.englishValueBefore: Bitcoin can be divided into 100 million smaller units called satoshis, making it perfect for transactions of any size from microtransactions to large purchases. Fine art cannot be divided - you cannot own a fraction of a painting or sell just part of a sculpture. This indivisibility limits investment flexibility and liquidity options.
entries.englishValue: Bitcoin divides into 100 million sats, making it perfect for any size transaction. You can't own a fraction of a painting or a corner of a sculpture without counterparty risk.
entries.currentValue: Bitcoin imatha kugawidwa kukhala zigawo 100 miliyoni zomwe zimatchedwa satoshis, zomwe zimapangitsa kukhala yabwino pa malonda a kukula kulikonse. Zojambula zapamwamba singagawidwe.
entries.targetTranslation: Bitcoin imagawanika m'magawo 100 miliyoni a satoshi, yokwanira kugwiritsa ntchito kulikonse. Simungakhale ndi kachigawo ka chithunzi kapena ngodya ya chosema popanda ngozi ya munthu wina.

entries.englishValueBefore: Bitcoin ownership and authenticity can be cryptographically verified on the blockchain by anyone with basic technical knowledge. Fine art requires expensive expert authentication, provenance research, and scientific analysis. Even with expert verification, forgeries regularly fool the art world, and authentication disputes can destroy an artwork's value overnight. Bitcoin, on the other hand, cannot be forged or counterfeited.
entries.englishValue: Bitcoin ownership and authenticity can be cryptographically verified by anyone on-chain. Art authentication is expensive, slow, and still routinely fooled by forgers — destroying an artwork's value overnight.
entries.currentValue: Umwini ndi kunena kwa Bitcoin kumatha kutsimikizidwa pa blockchain ndi aliyense. Zojambula zapamwamba zimafuna otsimikizira akatswiri odula ndipo zachinyengo nthawi zambiri zimanyenga dziko la zojambula.
entries.targetTranslation: Kukhala ndi Bitcoin ndi kutsimikizika kwake kungathe kutsimikiziridwa mwa cryptographic ndi aliyense pa blockchain. Kutsimikizika kwa zojambula ndi kokwera mtengo, kochedwa, ndipo amatchedwa kwambiri ndi opanga zabodza — kuwononga mtengo wa zojambula mwadzidzidzi.

entries.englishValueBefore: Bitcoin, when backed up properly, cannot be destroyed by floods, fires, earthquakes, hurricanes, theft, or other disasters. Fine art is vulnerable to all forms of physical destruction and deterioration. Even with expensive climate-controlled storage and comprehensive insurance, artworks can be damaged by environmental factors, accidents, or natural disasters, potentially losing all value.
entries.englishValue: Bitcoin, backed up properly, survives floods, fires, earthquakes, and theft. Fine art is vulnerable to every form of physical destruction, and insurance rarely covers it all.
entries.currentValue: Bitcoin, ikasungidwa bwino, singawonongeke ndi madzi, moto, zivomezi, mphepo, kuba, kapena masoka ena. Zojambula zapamwamba zili pa chiwopsezo cha kuwonongeka kwa mtundu uliwonse.
entries.targetTranslation: Bitcoin yokweza moyenera ikhoza kupulumuka pa madzi osefukira, moto, chivomerezi, ndi kuba. Zojambula zapamwamba zili zovuta ku mtundu uliwonse wa kuwonongeka kwa thupi, ndipo inshuwalansi sikukwanira pa zonse.

entries.englishValueBefore: Bitcoin can be bought and sold by anyone with internet access and a small amount of money to invest. Fine art investment is largely limited to wealthy collectors due to high minimum prices, exclusive auction access, storage requirements, insurance costs, and the specialized knowledge needed to navigate the art market successfully.
entries.englishValue: Anyone with an internet connection and a little money can buy Bitcoin. Fine art investment is effectively limited to wealthy collectors with auction access and specialized knowledge.
entries.currentValue: Bitcoin imatha kugulidwa ndi kugulitsidwa ndi aliyense wokhala ndi intaneti ndi ndalama zing'onozing'ono. Chikayikidwe cha zojambula zapamwamba ndi cha anthu olemera chifukwa cha mitengo yokwera.
entries.targetTranslation: Aliyense amene ali ndi internet ndi ndalama zochepa akhoza kugula Bitcoin. Kugula zojambula zapamwamba kuli kochepa kwa osonkhanitsa olemera okha okhala ndi mwayi wa auction ndi luso lapadera.

entries.englishValueBefore: Because Bitcoin is digital, it can be sent almost instantly for very low fees by anyone with an Internet connection. Because Gold is physical, it cannot be moved across the Internet and must be physically shipped to transfer ownership.
entries.englishValue: Bitcoin can be sent instantly over the internet for low fees. Gold must be physically shipped to transfer ownership.
entries.currentValue: Chifukwa Bitcoin ndi yadigitala, imatha kutumizidwa msanga ndi malipiro ochepa ndi aliyense amene ali ndi intaneti. Chifukwa Golide ndi chinthu chamaonekedwe, siingayendetsedwe pa intaneti ndipo iyenera kutumizidwa pamanjanja kuti uchikhale mwini.
entries.targetTranslation: Bitcoin imatha kutumizidwa pomwepo pa internet ndi ndalama zochepa. Golide iyenera kutumizidwa mwa thupi kuti isinthidwe ena.

entries.englishValueBefore: Bitcoin is a digitally native asset, which means you can transfer full ownership of it over the Internet. Some companies offer the ability to buy gold online without receiving the actual physical gold, instead trusting the company to hold the gold for you. This is more like a Digital IOU since you only own a promise from the company instead of the actual asset.
entries.englishValue: Bitcoin is a digitally native asset you can transfer over the internet. Online gold is a Digital IOU — you only own a promise from a custodian, not the metal itself.
entries.currentValue: Bitcoin ndi chuma chadigitala kwenizeni, kutanthauza kuti mutha kupereka umwini wonse pa intaneti. Makampani ena amapereka mwayi wogula golide pa intaneti popanda kulandira golideyo, m'malo mwake kukhulupirira kampaniyo kuti asunga golideyo. Izi zili ngati IOU yadigitala chifukwa muli ndi lonjezo la kampaniyo osati chuma chenichenicho.
entries.targetTranslation: Bitcoin ndi chuma cha digito chomwe mungatumize pa internet. Golide pa intaneti ndi IOU ya Digital — muli ndi lonjezo lokha kuchokera kwa wosungira, osati golide weniweni.

entries.englishValueBefore: Bitcoin has a hard cap of 21 Million BTC that will ever exist.
entries.englishValue: Bitcoin has a hard cap of 21 million BTC. Gold's supply grows about 1.6% per year, shrinking your slice — less than fiat
entries.currentValue: Bitcoin ili ndi malire olimba a Bitcoin 21 Miliyoni yomwe idzakhaleko.
entries.targetTranslation: Bitcoin ili ndi malire akhwawakhwa a 21 miliyoni ya BTC. Kuchuluka kwa golide kumakula pafupifupi 1.6% pachaka, kuchepetsa gawo lanu — kosakwana

entries.englishValueBefore: New gold supply is pulled out of the ground each year, resulting in inflation of the total supply. It's estimated that the total supply of gold increases by about 1.6% per year, which means your slice of the pie shrinks by 1.6% per year.
entries.englishValue: inflation
entries.currentValue: Golide yatsopano imachotsedwa pansi chaka chilichonse, zomwe zimapangitsa kukwera kwa kuchuluka. Zikuwoneka kuti kuchuluka kwa golide kumakwera pafupifupi 1.6% pachaka, kutanthauza kuti gawo lanu la keiki limachepa 1.6% pachaka.
entries.targetTranslation: kukwera kwa mitengo

entries.englishValueBefore: This is less than fiat inflation, but still inflation.
entries.englishValue: — but still inflation.
entries.currentValue: Izi ndi zochepa kuposa kukwera kwa ndalama za boma, koma kukwera kumene.
entries.targetTranslation: kwa fiat — koma chikadali kukwera kwa mitengo.

entries.englishValueBefore: Gold has an elastic supply, meaning that as the price of gold rises, there is a greater incentive to mine more gold. This often puts downward pressure on the gold price as new mines come online.
entries.englishValue: When gold prices rise, more gold gets mined, pushing the price back down. Bitcoin's supply is inelastic — no matter how high the price goes, there will only ever be 21 million.
entries.currentValue: Golide ili ndi kuchuluka komata, kutanthauza kuti mtengo wa golide ukukwera, pali chilimbikitso chachikulu kufukula golide zambiri. Izi nthawi zambiri zimapanikiza mtengo wa golide pansi pomwe magodoro atsopano akuyamba kugwira ntchito.
entries.targetTranslation: Mtengo wa golide ukakwera, golide yochuluka imafukulidwa, kupangitsa mtengo wake kutsika. Kuchuluka kwa Bitcoin sikusinthasintha — ngakhale mtengo wakwera kwambiri, idzakhalapo basi 21 miliyoni.

entries.englishValueBefore: The Bitcoin network is decentralized.
entries.englishValue: Tens of thousands of independent nodes validate the Bitcoin network. Most physical gold sits in a handful of large custodian vaults.
entries.currentValue: Netiweki ya Bitcoin yogawidwa.
entries.targetTranslation: Makumi ambiri a node odziimira amatsimikizira netiweki ya Bitcoin. Golide yambiri yathupi imakhala m'zipinda zochepa zazikulu zosungira.

entries.englishValueBefore: With Bitcoin, it's incredibly easy to verify that you have real Bitcoin by taking self-custody of your coins and running a full node.
entries.englishValue: Anyone can verify real Bitcoin by running a full node — it's just an app. Verifying physical gold requires melting it down; the inside could be tungsten.
entries.currentValue: Ndi Bitcoin, n'kosavuta kwambiri kutsimikizira kuti muli ndi Bitcoin yeniyeni pokusunga ndi kuthamanga node yathunthu.
entries.targetTranslation: Aliyense akhoza kutsimikizira Bitcoin yowona pothamangitsa full node — ndi pulogalamu yokha. Kutsimikizira golide yathupi kumafunika kuyiwala; mkati mwake mukhoza kukhala tungsten.

entries.englishValueBefore: Just like there are 100 cents in 1 dollar, there are 100,000,000 sats in 1 Bitcoin. This enables Bitcoin to be used for all scales of purchases, including microtransactions as small as a few cents.
entries.englishValue: Bitcoin divides into 100 million sats, making it perfect for any size purchase. Gold can't be easily divided for small transactions.
entries.currentValue: Monga momwe pali ma senti 100 mu dola 1, pali sats 100,000,000 mu Bitcoin 1. Izi zimathandiza Bitcoin kugwiritsidwa ntchito pa malonda aliwonse, kuphatikiza malonda ang'onoang'ono a masenti ochepa.
entries.targetTranslation: Bitcoin imagawanika m'magawo 100 miliyoni a satoshi, yokwanira kugula kulikonse. Golide singagawane mosavuta pa zochita zazing'ono.

entries.englishValueBefore: Bitcoin can be moved anywhere in the world instantly over the internet. Real estate is permanently fixed to a specific location and cannot be relocated, making it vulnerable to local economic conditions, natural disasters, and political instability.
entries.englishValue: Bitcoin moves anywhere in the world instantly. Real estate is fixed to one location and exposed to local economic, political, and natural risks.
entries.currentValue: Bitcoin imatha kuyendetsedwa kulikonse padziko lonse pa intaneti nthawi yomweyo. Nyumba zili pamalo okhazikika ndipo singayendetsedwe.
entries.targetTranslation: Bitcoin imayenda kulikonse padziko lapansi pomwepo. Malo amamangidwa kumalo amodzi ndipo ali pachiwopsezo cha zachuma, ndale, ndi zachilengedwe za m'deralo.

entries.englishValueBefore: Bitcoin can be divided into 100 million smaller units called satoshis, making it perfect for transactions of any size. Real estate cannot be easily divided - you can't sell just the kitchen of your house or buy half a bedroom.
entries.englishValue: Bitcoin divides into 100 million sats. Real estate can't be partly sold — you can't offload just the kitchen or buy half a bedroom.
entries.currentValue: Bitcoin imatha kugawidwa kukhala zigawo 100 miliyoni zomwe zimatchedwa satoshis. Nyumba singagawidwe mosavuta - simungathe kugulitsa khitchini yokha ya nyumba yanu.
entries.targetTranslation: Bitcoin imagawanika m'magawo 100 miliyoni a satoshi. Malo singagulitsidwe pang'ono — simungagulitse khitchini kapena kugula theka la chipinda.

entries.englishValueBefore: Bitcoin operates on a decentralized network that no government can control. Real estate is subject to extensive government regulation including rent control, eviction moratoriums, zoning laws, and eminent domain where governments can seize your property.
entries.englishValue: Bitcoin operates on a decentralized network that no government can control. Real estate is heavily regulated — zoning, rent control, eminent domain, and seizure all apply.
entries.currentValue: Bitcoin imagwira ntchito pa netiweki yogawidwa yomwe palibe boma limene lingathe kulamulira. Nyumba zimalamulira ndi malamulo ambiri a boma kuphatikiza kulamulira malipiro a lendi, malamulo a kukhazikitsa, ndi eminent domain pomwe maboma amatha kulanda katundu wanu.
entries.targetTranslation: Bitcoin imagwira ntchito pa netiweki yopanda wolamulira yomwe palibe boma lingathe kulamulira. Malo amalamulidwa kwambiri — zoning, kuwongolera renti, eminent domain, ndi kulanda zonse zikugwira ntchito.

entries.englishValueBefore: Bitcoin requires no maintenance - it exists as digital code on a network. Real estate requires constant upkeep including repairs, renovations, property management, insurance, and dealing with tenants if rented.
entries.englishValue: Bitcoin requires no upkeep. Real estate demands repairs, renovations, insurance, property management, and tenant issues.
entries.currentValue: Bitcoin sikufuna kukonza chilichonse - imakhala ngati khodi yadigitala pa netiweki. Nyumba zimafuna kukonza nthawi zonse kuphatikiza kukonzakonza, kukonzanso, kusamalira, inshulansi, ndi kugwira ntchito ndi olipira ngati zikubwereketsa.
entries.targetTranslation: Bitcoin saifuna kusamalidwa. Malo amafunika kukonza, kusintha, inshuwalansi, kasamalidwe ka katundu, ndi mavuto a omwe akukhalamo.

entries.englishValueBefore: Bitcoin has no ongoing taxes - you only pay capital gains when you sell. Real estate is subject to annual property taxes that must be paid regardless of whether the property generates income, effectively forcing you to rent your own property from the government forever.
entries.englishValue: Bitcoin has no ongoing taxes — you only pay capital gains when you sell. Real estate owes annual property taxes regardless of income.
entries.currentValue: Bitcoin ilibe misonkho yopitirira - mumalipira capital gains mukagulitsa kokha. Nyumba zimaweruzidwa misonkho ya katundu iliyonse yomwe iyenera kulipidwa mosasamala ngati katundowo ukubweretsa ndalama.
entries.targetTranslation: Bitcoin ilibe misonkho yopitilizika — mukulipira capital gain pakangogulitsa. Malo amalipira misonkho ya katundu chaka chilichonse mosaganizira ndalama.

entries.englishValueBefore: Bitcoin, when backed up properly, cannot be destroyed by floods, fires, earthquakes, hurricanes, or other natural disasters. Real estate is vulnerable to all forms of physical destruction and requires expensive insurance that may not fully cover losses.
entries.englishValue: Bitcoin, backed up properly, survives fire, flood, and earthquake. Real estate is vulnerable to every disaster, and insurance rarely covers it all.
entries.currentValue: Bitcoin, ikasungidwa bwino, singawonongeke ndi madzi, moto, zivomezi, mphepo, kapena masoka ena achilengedwe. Nyumba zili pa chiwopsezo cha kuwonongeka kwa mtundu uliwonse.
entries.targetTranslation: Bitcoin yokweza moyenera ikhoza kupulumuka pa moto, madzi osefukira, ndi chivomerezi. Malo ali pachiwopsezo cha tsoka lililonse, ndipo inshuwalansi sikufikira pa zonse.

entries.englishValueBefore: Every bitcoin is identical and interchangeable - one bitcoin equals one bitcoin anywhere in the world. Every piece of real estate is unique with different locations, conditions, and characteristics, making it difficult to price and compare properties.
entries.englishValue: Every bitcoin is identical and interchangeable. Every property is unique, making pricing and comparisons difficult.
entries.currentValue: Bitcoin iliyonse ndi yofanana ndi ina iliyonse - bitcoin imodzi ndi bitcoin imodzi kulikonse padziko lonse. Nyumba iliyonse ndi yapadera ndi malo, kuyendera, ndi makhalidwe osiyanasiyana.
entries.targetTranslation: Bitcoin iliyonse imafanana ndipo ingasinthidwe. Malo aliwonse ndi apadera, kupangitsa kupanga mitengo ndi kuyerekeza kovuta.

entries.englishValueBefore: Bitcoin can be bought and sold 24/7 by anyone with internet access anywhere in the world. Real estate sales are limited to local buyers, require lengthy processes with lawyers and agents, and can take months to complete.
entries.englishValue: Bitcoin trades globally 24/7 by anyone with internet access. Real estate sales are limited to local buyers and can take months of paperwork to close.
entries.currentValue: Bitcoin imatha kugulidwa ndi kugulitsidwa 24/7 ndi aliyense wokhala ndi intaneti kulikonse padziko lonse. Kugulitsa nyumba kumadaliridwa ndi ogula akomweko, kumafuna nthawi yaitali ndi malamulo ambiri.
entries.targetTranslation: Bitcoin imagulitsidwa padziko lonse 24/7 ndi aliyense amene ali ndi internet. Kugulitsa malo kuli kochepa kwa ogula a m'derali ndipo kungatenge miyezi yambiri yokhala ndi mapepala.

entries.englishValueBefore: Bitcoin enables direct individual ownership without intermediaries, promoting financial sovereignty for everyone. Buying real estate as an investment beyond your primary residence contributes to the financialization of housing, treating homes as commodities rather than shelter. This drives up prices, reduces affordability for families, and contributes to the housing and homelessness crisis affecting many countries today.
entries.englishValue: Bitcoin enables direct individual ownership for anyone. Buying real estate as an investment beyond your primary residence drives up housing prices, reducing affordability and fueling the housing crisis.
entries.currentValue: Bitcoin imalimbikitsa umwini wachindunji popanda anthu apakati. Kugula nyumba ngati chikayikidwe kupitirira nyumba yanu yaikulu kumathandizira kulimbitsa nyumba ngati katundu, zomwe zimakweza mitengo ndi kuchepetsa mwayi wa mabanja, ndipo zikuthandizira vuto la nyumba ndi kusowa kwa pokhala padziko lino lero.
entries.targetTranslation: Bitcoin imathandiza kukhala ndi okha kwa aliyense. Kugula malo ngati ndalama kupitirira nyumba yanu yayikulu kumakulitsa mitengo ya nyumba, kuchepetsa kukwanitsa kwa anthu ena ndikupangitsa zovuta zanyumba.

entries.englishValueBefore: When you own Bitcoin, you have direct ownership of the asset itself. When you own stocks, you own a share of a company, which means your investment depends on the company's performance, management decisions, and business success.
entries.englishValue: Bitcoin is a direct asset you own outright. Stocks are shares in a company — their value depends on management, performance, and decisions you can't control.
entries.currentValue: Mukakhala ndi Bitcoin, muli ndi umwini wachindunji wa chumachi. Mukakhala ndi ma share, muli ndi gawo la kampani, kutanthauza kuti chikayikidwe chanu chidalira momwe kampaniyo ikuyendera, zisankho za olamulira, ndi kupambana kwa bizinesiyo.
entries.targetTranslation: Bitcoin ndi chuma chachindunji chomwe muli nacho ndi kwathunthu. Masheya ndi magawo a kampani — mtengo wake umadalira utsogoleri, ntchito, ndi zisankho zomwe inu simungazilamulire.

entries.englishValueBefore: Bitcoin operates on a decentralized network with no single point of failure. Stock investments are subject to key person risk - if the CEO or other critical leaders leave, get sick, or make poor decisions, your investment can suffer significantly. Companies depend heavily on their leadership teams.
entries.englishValue: Bitcoin has no CEO and no single point of failure. Stocks depend heavily on leadership — one bad decision or departure can tank the price.
entries.currentValue: Bitcoin imagwira ntchito pa netiweki yogawidwa yopanda malo ovutikira amodzi. Ma share akuyikidwa ku chiwopsezo cha anthu ofunika - ngati mkulu wa kampani atachoka, kudwala, kapena kupanga zisankho zoyipa, chikayikidwe chanu chikhoza kuvutika kwambiri.
entries.targetTranslation: Bitcoin ilibe CEO ndipo ilibe malo amodzi olephera. Masheya amadalira kwambiri utsogoleri — chisankho chimodzi cholakwika kapena kuchoka kungapangitse mtengo kugwa.

entries.englishValueBefore: Bitcoin's price is determined purely by market supply and demand. Stock prices are often evaluated using P/E ratios (Price-to-Earnings), which show how much investors pay for each dollar of company earnings. High P/E ratios can indicate overvalued stocks, making it harder to determine fair value.
entries.englishValue: Bitcoin's price comes from open global markets. Stock valuations rely on metrics like P/E ratios that can mask overpriced shares.
entries.currentValue: Mtengo wa Bitcoin umasankhidwa ndi kufunika ndi kuchuluka pa msika. Mitengo ya ma share nthawi zambiri imawunikiridwa pogwiritsa ntchito ma P/E ratio (Mtengo-ku-Phindu), omwe amaonetsa ndalama zomwe ogula amalipira pa dola iliyonse ya phindu la kampani.
entries.targetTranslation: Mtengo wa Bitcoin umachokera ku misika ya padziko lonse yotseguka. Mtengo wa masheya umadalira muyezo monga ma P/E ratio omwe akhoza kubisa masheya okwera mtengo kwambiri.

entries.englishValueBefore: Bitcoin trades 24 hours a day, 7 days a week on global exchanges.
entries.englishValue: Bitcoin trades 24/7 around the world. Stock markets are only open during business hours on weekdays.

entries.targetTranslation: Bitcoin imagulitsidwa 24/7 padziko lonse. Misika ya masheya imatsegulidwa pa nthawi za bizinesi pa masiku a sabata.

entries.englishValueBefore: Bitcoin is a fixed supply asset with a hard cap of 21 million Bitcoin that will ever exist. This makes it a great inflation hedge. Stocks have variable performance against inflation - some companies do well during inflationary periods while others struggle. There's no guarantee that any particular stock will protect against inflation.
entries.englishValue: Bitcoin's fixed supply makes it a reliable inflation hedge. Some stocks beat inflation, others don't — there's no guarantee.

entries.englishValueBefore: Bitcoin is an open network that anyone can join and use without permission. Credit card networks like Visa are closed systems controlled by financial institutions that can deny access to anyone they choose.
entries.englishValue: Bitcoin is an open network anyone can join and use without permission. Visa is a closed system controlled by financial institutions that can deny access — especially to the unbanked and underbanked.

entries.englishValueBefore: Accepting Bitcoin has many benefits like accepting payments with lower fees & getting more customers.
entries.englishValue: The simplest way to accept Bitcoin is with a hybrid wallet that automatically sells 100% of the Bitcoin you receive for dollars (or your local currency) the instant a payment comes in.
entries.currentValue: Kulandira Bitcoin kuli ndi phindu zambiri monga kulandira malipiro ndi malipiro ochepa ndi kupeza makasitomala ambiri.

entries.englishValue: With this setup, your books look exactly like they do today — the final number is in dollars, every time. No cost basis, no capital gains, no new spreadsheets.
entries.currentValue: Ngati mugwiritsa ntchito Chikwama Chosakaniza kuchokera ku Gaidi yathu ya Zikwama ndipo muzigulitsa mwachindunji 100% ya Bitcoin yomwe mwalandira kukhala madola, simukufunika kusintha chilichonse mu kulemba ndalama kwanu.

entries.englishValueBefore: Tracking your cost basis is going to be the biggest difference between accounting for dollars and accounting for Bitcoin. Even if you view your business entirely in terms of Bitcoin, you need to report the dollar value of each transaction on your taxes.
entries.englishValue: Some businesses choose to keep a portion of the Bitcoin they receive instead of auto-converting it all. If that's you, the main extra step is tracking your cost basis — the dollar value of each Bitcoin payment on the day you received it.
entries.currentValue: Kutsatira mtengo wanu woyambirira ndi kusiyana kwakukulu pakati pa kulemba ndalama kwa madola ndi kulemba ndalama kwa Bitcoin. Ngakhale mumaona bizinesi yanu mu Bitcoin, mukuyenera kunena mtengo wa madola wa machitidwe aliwonse pa misonkho yanu.
entries.targetTranslation: Mabizinesi ena amasankha kusunga gawo la Bitcoin yomwe alandira m'malo mosintha zonse mwadzidzidzi. Ngati ndi inu, sitepe yowonjezera ndi kulemba mtengo wapakhomo wanu — mtengo wa dola wa tsiku lomwe Bitcoin idalandiridwa.

entries.englishValue: Even if you think of your business entirely in Bitcoin, most tax authorities still want the dollar value reported. The good news: it's just two numbers per transaction — the amount of Bitcoin received and its dollar value on that day.

entries.targetTranslation: Ngakhale mukuganiza za bizinesi yanu m'Bitcoin, akuluakulu a misonkho amafuna kuti mtengo wa dola udziwike. Nkhani yabwino — nambala ziwiri zokha pa malonda aliwonse — kuchuluka kwa Bitcoin yolandiridwa ndi mtengo wake wa dola pa tsikulo.

entries.englishValue: Bitcoin has a fixed supply of 21 million coins. No government, bank, or company can print more of it. Your Bitcoin savings hold their value over time instead of quietly losing it.

entries.englishValueBefore: Multiple US banks have collapsed in the past few years due to bank runs.
entries.englishValue: Multiple U.S. banks have collapsed in recent years because of bank runs. When too many customers tried to withdraw at once, the banks didn't have the cash to pay everyone back.
entries.currentValue: Mabanki angapo ku United States agwa m'zaka zapitazi chifukwa cha kuthawa kwa anthu kumabanki.
entries.targetTranslation: Mabanki angapo a U.S. agwa m'zaka zaposachedwa chifukwa cha kuthawira ku banki. Pamene makasitomala ambiri ayesa kuchotsa nthawi imodzi, mabanki sanali ndi ndalama zokwanira kuwabwezera anthu onse.

entries.englishValueBefore: Instead of just holding your money for you, banks invest and lend out your money. If those investments don't do well, they don't have enough to pay you back.
entries.englishValue: Instead of just holding your money, banks lend and invest most of it. If those investments go bad — or if depositors lose confidence — the bank can fail, and your deposits can be frozen or lost.
entries.currentValue: M'malo mosungira ndalama zanu, mabanki amayika ndalama zanu ndi kubwereketsa. Ngati zikayikidwezo sizinayende bwino, alibe ndalama zokwanira kukubwezerani.
entries.targetTranslation: M'malo mosunga ndalama zanu basi, mabanki amakongoza ndi kuyika ndalama zambiri. Ngati ma investment amenewo achitidwa zoyipa — kapena ngati osungira ndalama achotsa chikhulupiriro — banki ikhoza kulephera, ndipo ndalama zomwe mwayika zikhoza kutsekedwa kapena kutayika.

entries.englishValueBefore: And the FDIC insurance fund only has $1 for every $100 they're insuring.
entries.englishValue: With Bitcoin, you can hold your own money directly in your own wallet. No bank. No intermediary. No bank run.
entries.currentValue: Ndipo inshulansi ya FDIC ili ndi $1 yokha pa $100 iliyonse yomwe akuteteza.
entries.targetTranslation: Ndi Bitcoin, mukhoza kusunga ndalama zanu mwachindunji mu chikwama chanu. Palibe banki. Palibe wapakatikati. Palibe kuthawira ku banki.

entries.englishValueBefore: Unlike traditional financial networks, Bitcoin doesn't require permission to be used.
entries.englishValue: Unlike credit cards, PayPal, or traditional bank accounts, Bitcoin doesn't require anyone's permission to use.
entries.currentValue: Mosiyana ndi maukonde a ndalama achikhalidwe, Bitcoin sikufuna chilolezo kuti igwiritsidwe ntchito.
entries.targetTranslation: Mosiyana ndi makhadi ongongoletsa, PayPal, kapena akaunti za mabanki, Bitcoin saifuna chilolezo cha aliyense kuti igwiritsidwe ntchito.

entries.englishValueBefore: That means no one can stop you from using Bitcoin for any reason. It's the first financial network you can use without fear of censorship or seizure.
entries.englishValue: No one can freeze your account, block a payment, or cut you off from the network. It's the first financial system in history you can use freely, without fear of censorship or seizure.
entries.currentValue: Izi zikutanthauza kuti palibe amene angakuletseni kugwiritsa ntchito Bitcoin pa chifukwa chilichonse. Ndi netiweki yoyamba ya ndalama yomwe mungagwiritse ntchito popanda mantha a kuletsa kapena kulanda.
entries.targetTranslation: Palibe amene angatseke akaunti yanu, kuletsa malipiro, kapena kukulekanitsani ndi netiweki. Ndi dongosolo loyamba lazachuma m'mbiri lomwe mungagwiritse ntchito mwaufulu, popanda mantha a kuletsedwa kapena kulanda.

entries.englishValueBefore: Bitcoin is a misunderstood technology that is building a better world.
entries.englishValue: Bitcoin is often misunderstood, but it's quietly doing a lot of good in the world.
entries.currentValue: Bitcoin ndi teknoloji yomwe anthu ambiri samaimvetsetsa koma ikumanga dziko labwino.
entries.targetTranslation: Bitcoin nthawi zambiri samvetsedwa, koma ikuchita zabwino zambiri padziko mwa kakhalidwe.

entries.englishValueBefore: Bitcoin has enabled human rights activists to fight for freedom, reduced global methane emissions, saved national parks, and so much more.

entries.englishValue: Bitcoin is a full-reserve system. You're not depositing your money in a bank. You are your own bank. There's no lending out your money without your knowledge because you are the only one who can access your money.

entries.englishValue: Accepting Bitcoin at your business doesn't have to complicate your accounting. Here's the short version — plus the tools and pros to make it painless.
entries.targetTranslation: Kulandira Bitcoin m'bizinesi yanu sikuyenera kupangitsa kasamalidwe ka ndalama kuti kakhale kovuta. Apa pali baibulo losavuta ndi zida ndi akatswiri omwe amapangitsa kukhala kotetezeka.

entries.englishValue: If you already accept cash or card, adding Bitcoin to your business books is simpler than it looks. You have two paths: auto-convert every Bitcoin payment to dollars the moment it arrives (no new accounting needed), or keep some as Bitcoin (a few extra numbers to track).
entries.targetTranslation: Ngati mukulandira ndalama zenizeni kapena makhadi kale, kuonjezera Bitcoin m'mabuku anu kuli kosavuta kuposa momwe mukuganizira. Pali njira ziwiri — sinthani malipiro a Bitcoin kukhala dola mwadzidzidzi (palibe kasamalidwe katsopano), kapena sungani ena ngati Bitcoin (kuwonjezera mbali zochepa).

entries.englishValue: This guide walks you through both — so you can pick the one that fits your business and start accepting Bitcoin with confidence.

entries.englishValue: Bitcoin gives your business a faster, cheaper, more private way to get paid. No middlemen. No chargebacks. No contracts. Just money that settles in seconds, directly from your customers to you.
entries.targetTranslation: Bitcoin imapatsa bizinesi yanu njira yofulumira, yotsika mtengo, komanso yachinsinsi yolandilira ndalama. Palibe apakati. Palibe ma chargeback. Palibe mapangano. Ndalama yokhazikika kuchokera kwa kasitomala kupita kwa inu mu masekondi ochepa.

entries.englishValue: Below is the short version of why Bitcoin is good for business — and below that, every resource you need to start accepting it today.
entries.targetTranslation: Pansipa pali baibulo losavuta lokhudza chifukwa chake Bitcoin ndi yabwino kwa bizinesi — ndi zothandizira zonse zomwe mukufunika kuti muyambe kulandira Bitcoin lero.

entries.targetTranslation: Zonse zomwe mukufunika kuti mulandire Bitcoin

entries.englishValue: Work through these resources at your own pace. Each one is a short, practical guide.
entries.targetTranslation: Sangalalani ndi zothandizirazi pa liwiro lanu. Iliyonse ndi gaidi yochepa, yothandiza yolimbitsidwa pa zochita.

entries.englishValue: Tell us about your business
entries.targetTranslation: Tiuzeni za bizinesi yanu

entries.englishValue: We only need a few details to get you listed. Address data is kept only long enough to submit your business to the maps.
entries.targetTranslation: Tikufuna zambiri zochepa kuti tikhale ndi mwayi wokulemba. Deta ya adilesi yanu imasungidwa kokha mokwanira nthawi yokulowetsa bizinesi yanu pa mapu.

entries.englishValue: List your business for free on BTC Map — the open, worldwide directory of Bitcoin-accepting merchants — so Bitcoiners nearby can find you and spend Bitcoin at your business.
entries.targetTranslation: Lembani bizinesi yanu mwaulere pa BTC Map — mndandanda wotseguka wa amalonda padziko lonse omwe amalandira Bitcoin — kuti ogwiritsa ntchito Bitcoin a m'derali apeze inu ndikugwiritsa ntchito Bitcoin pa bizinesi yanu.

entries.englishValue: Get your business on Bitcoin merchant maps
entries.targetTranslation: Lembani bizinesi yanu pa Mapu a Amalonda a Bitcoin

entries.englishValue: Bitcoiners actively look for places to spend. Getting your business on the map puts you in front of every Bitcoin user searching for somewhere to eat, shop, or stay nearby — at zero cost to you.
entries.targetTranslation: Anthu ogwiritsa ntchito Bitcoin amafufuza malo ogwiritsa ntchito ndalama zawo. Kuyika bizinesi yanu pa mapuwa kumakuyikani patsogolo pa wogwiritsa ntchito Bitcoin aliyense pafupi yemwe akufuna malo odyera, kugula, kapena kukhala — popanda mtengo kwa inu.

entries.englishValue: Just fill out the short form below and we'll submit your business to BTC Map and other Bitcoin merchant maps for you.
entries.targetTranslation: Dzazani fomu yosavuta pansipa ndipo tiyika bizinesi yanu pa BTC Map ndi mapu ena a amalonda a Bitcoin.

entries.englishValue: List your business for free on BTC Map and other Bitcoin merchant maps so Bitcoiners nearby can find you.
entries.targetTranslation: Lembani bizinesi yanu mwaulere pa BTC Map ndi mapu ena a amalonda a Bitcoin kuti ogwiritsa ntchito Bitcoin a m'derali akupezeni.

entries.englishValue: Your business will be listed on BTC Map and other Bitcoin merchant directories within 1 to 2 weeks. We review each submission by hand to keep the maps accurate.

entries.englishValue: Once your listing is live, Bitcoiners nearby can find your business and come spend Bitcoin there.
entries.targetTranslation: Mlandulo wanu ukatulutsidwa, ogwiritsa ntchito Bitcoin a m'derali akhoza kupeza bizinesi yanu ndi kuyamba kugwiritsa ntchito Bitcoin.

entries.englishValue: We'll create and publish your sticker files within 3 to 4 weeks. Once they're ready, you'll be able to download and print them for free from our sticker files page.
entries.targetTranslation: Tikupanga ndi kutulutsa mafayilo anu a zitikiti mu sabata 3–4. Akakhala okonzeka, mukhoza kutsitsa ndi kuwasindikiza mwaulere kuchokera tsamba lathu la mafayilo a zitikiti.

entries.englishValue: Sticker files are released in batches, so it may take a few weeks for your language to go live. Thanks for your patience!
entries.targetTranslation: Timatulutsa zitikiti m'magulu — chilankhulo chanu chikhoza kutenga sabata yochepa kuti chitulutsidwe. Zikomo chifukwa cha kupirira kwanu.

entries.targetTranslation: Zitikiti zanu zaulere za 'Bitcoin Imalandiridwa Pano' zikufika mu sabata 2–4 — mu envelopi yoyera yokhala ndi zitikiti 3.

entries.englishValue: Your stickers are on their way 🎉
entries.targetTranslation: Zitikiti zanu zikupita 🎉

entries.englishValue: If 3 stickers aren't enough for your business, feel free to request another free pack — or order in bulk from the same printer we use.
entries.targetTranslation: Ngati zitikiti 3 zilibe ku bizinesi yanu, mukhoza kupempha zambiri zaulere — kapena kuodola zambiri kuchokera kwa wosindikiza yemwe ife timagwiritsa ntchito.

entries.englishValue: Let your customers know you accept Bitcoin. Order a free pack of 'Bitcoin Accepted Here' stickers to put up at your business.
entries.targetTranslation: Uzeni makasitomala anu kuti mukulandira Bitcoin. Odolani paketi yaulere ya zitikiti za 'Bitcoin Imalandiridwa Pano' kuti muyike pa bizinesi yanu.

entries.englishValue: Free 'Bitcoin Accepted Here' stickers
entries.targetTranslation: Zitikiti zaulere za 'Bitcoin Imalandiridwa Pano'

entries.englishValue: Accepting Bitcoin is only half the job — your customers also need to know that you do. These small 'Bitcoin Accepted Here' stickers are designed to stick on your front door, register, menu, or anywhere else customers will see them before they pay.
entries.targetTranslation: Kulandira Bitcoin ndi theka chabe la ntchito — makasitomala anu ayenera kudziwa kuti mukulandira nayo. Zitikiti za 'Bitcoin Imalandiridwa Pano' zinapangidwa kuti ziyikidwe pa khomo, kasha, menyu, kapena malo aliwonse omwe makasitomala adzaona malipiroli.

entries.englishValue: We'll mail you a free pack anywhere in the USA or Canada, or you can print your own anywhere in the world.
entries.targetTranslation: Tikutumiza mwaulere kulikonse ku USA kapena Canada — kapena mukhoza kusindikiza nokha kulikonse padziko lapansi.

entries.englishValue: You can print your own 'Bitcoin Accepted Here' stickers, no matter where you live. Click your language below to download the sticker files and printing instructions.
entries.targetTranslation: Mukhoza kusindikiza nokha zitikiti za 'Bitcoin Imalandiridwa Pano' kulikonse komwe muli. Dinani pa chilankhulo chanu pansipa kuti mutsitse mafayilo a zitikiti ndi malangizo.

entries.targetTranslation: Dzadzani fomu yomwe ili pansipa kuti mupemphe mafayilo a zitikiti mu chilankhulo chanu cha m'derali. Tikukuuzani akakhala okonzeka.

entries.englishValue: All Bitcoin wallets are interoperable — pick the one that fits your business. Free, instant settlement, no chargebacks.
entries.targetTranslation: Zikwama zonse za Bitcoin zimalumikizana — sankhani yomwe ikugwirizana ndi bizinesi yanu. Yaulere, kutsiriza pomwepo, palibe ma chargeback.

entries.englishValue: Breez — Bitcoin-only Lightning wallet
entries.targetTranslation: Breez — Chikwama cha Lightning chodzipangira chovomerezedwa ndi mabizinesi

entries.englishValue: IBEX — Lightning payments infrastructure
entries.targetTranslation: IBEX — Maziko a malipiro a Lightning

entries.englishValue: Zaprite — Bitcoin invoicing for businesses
entries.targetTranslation: Zaprite — Mabilu a Bitcoin a mabizinesi

entries.englishValue: Bitcoin wallets are free. Pick one that fits your business — in-person, online, or invoice-based — and start accepting Bitcoin in minutes.
entries.targetTranslation: Zikwama zaulere za Bitcoin za mabizinesi. Sankhani yomwe ikugwirizana ndi bizinesi yanu — mwaokha, pa intaneti, kapena yobikidwa pa bilu — ndipo yambani kulandira Bitcoin mu mphindi zochepa.

entries.englishValue: Wallets for invoice-based businesses
entries.targetTranslation: Zikwama za mabizinesi okhalitsa ma bilu

entries.englishValue: If you invoice clients (consulting, freelancing, B2B services), use a wallet built around invoicing. Your client pays a Bitcoin invoice in a couple of clicks.
entries.targetTranslation: Ngati mukutumiza ma bilu kwa olemba upangiri, antchito odzipangira, kapena ntchito za B2B, gwiritsani ntchito chikwama chopangidwira kupanga ma bilu. Kasitomala wanu akhoza kulipira bilu ya Bitcoin ndi madinde ochepa.

entries.englishValue: Wallets for businesses with multiple employees
entries.targetTranslation: Zikwama za mabizinesi okhala ndi antchito ambiri

entries.englishValue: If you have a team taking payments at the register, choose a wallet that supports multiple employee logins — so every employee gets their own PIN and you keep a clean audit trail of who took which payment.
entries.targetTranslation: Ngati muli ndi gulu lolandirira ndalama pa kasha, sankhani chikwama chokhala ndi mwayi kwa antchito ambiri — wantchito aliyense amapeza PIN yake yokha, ndipo mumakhalabe ndi maumbiri akumva omveka kuti ndani analandila chiyani.

entries.englishValue: Wallets for online businesses
entries.targetTranslation: Zikwama za mabizinesi a pa intaneti

entries.englishValue: Selling on a website? These wallets plug into your online store and accept Bitcoin from any customer, anywhere in the world — no chargebacks, no merchant account required.
entries.targetTranslation: Mukugulitsa pa webusayiti? Zikwamazi zimalumikizana ndi malo anu ogulitsa pa intaneti ndipo zimalandira Bitcoin kuchokera kwa makasitomala kulikonse padziko lapansi — popanda ma chargeback, palibe akaunti ya wamalonda yofunika.

entries.englishValue: Wallets for individually-owned businesses
entries.targetTranslation: Zikwama za mabizinesi a munthu m'modzi

entries.englishValue: If you run a shop, café, studio, or service on your own, any of these wallets will work. Pick based on whether you want to keep payments in Bitcoin or auto-convert part of each payment to your local currency.
entries.targetTranslation: Ngati mukuyendetsa malo ogulitsa, malo ogulitsa khofi, studio, kapena ntchito mwekha, zikwamazi zikugwira ntchito. Sankhani malingana ndi ngati mukufuna kusunga malipiro ngati Bitcoin kapena kusintha mwadzidzidzi ena kukhala ndalama yakuderali.

entries.englishValue: Strike Business lets you accept Bitcoin and Lightning payments with zero fees and instant settlement. Supports in-person, online, and invoice-based payments with optional auto-conversion to your local currency.
entries.targetTranslation: Strike Business ndiyo yomwe imalimbikitsidwa nthawi zambiri kwa mabizinesi a USA chifukwa cha kuphweka kwake — imasintha 100% ya Bitcoin yomwe mwalandira kukhala madola mwadzidzidzi.

entries.englishValue: Lower fees, more for the business
entries.targetTranslation: Ndalama zochepa, zambiri kwa bizinesi

entries.englishValue: Bitcoin payments skip the banks and credit card companies that take 2–3% from every sale. The business keeps more of what you pay — which often means better prices and better service for you.
entries.targetTranslation: Malipiro a Bitcoin amapeweka mabanki ndi makampani a makhadi omwe amatenga 2–3% pa kugulitsa kulikonse. Bizinesi imasunga zambiri za zomwe mukulipira — zomwe nthawi zambiri zikutanthauza mitengo yabwino ndi ntchito yabwino kwa inu.

entries.englishValue: Instant settlement, no chargebacks
entries.targetTranslation: Kutsiriza pomwepo, palibe ma chargeback

entries.englishValue: Bitcoin payments settle in seconds, directly from your wallet to the business. There's no waiting days for a bank to release funds, and no costly chargeback disputes — so the business can focus on serving customers instead of fighting fraud.
entries.targetTranslation: Malipiro a Bitcoin amatsiriza mu masekondi, mwachindunji kuchokera mu chikwama chanu kupita ku bizinesi. Palibe kudikira masiku banki kuti ipereke ndalama, ndipo palibe mikangano yokwera mtengo ya chargeback — kotero bizinesi ikhoza kuyang'anira kupereka ntchito kwa makasitomala m'malo molimbana ndi chinyengo.

entries.englishValue: Free to accept, open to everyone
entries.targetTranslation: Yaulere kulandirira, yotseguka kwa aliyense

entries.englishValue: There are no contracts, monthly fees, or setup costs for a business to accept Bitcoin. And millions of Bitcoin users around the world actively seek out merchants that accept it — giving this business free exposure to new customers.
entries.targetTranslation: Palibe mapangano, ndalama za mwezi, kapena ndalama zoyikira kuti bizinesi ilandire Bitcoin. Ndipo mamiliyoni a ogwiritsa ntchito Bitcoin padziko lonse amafufuza amalonda omwe amalandira — zomwe zimapereka bizinesi iyi mwayi waulere wa makasitomala atsopano.

entries.englishValue: Run a business and want to start accepting Bitcoin?
entries.targetTranslation: Mukuyendetsa bizinesi ndipo mukufuna kuyamba kulandira Bitcoin?

entries.targetTranslation: Onani momwe imagwirira ntchito →

entries.englishValue: Why Bitcoin is great for this business
entries.targetTranslation: Chifukwa chake Bitcoin ndi yabwino kwa bizinesi iyi

entries.englishValue: Accepting Bitcoin lets a business keep more of every sale, get paid instantly with no chargebacks, and reach a global audience of Bitcoin users — all with zero contracts and zero monthly fees.
entries.targetTranslation: Kulandira Bitcoin kumalola bizinesi kusunga zambiri za kugulitsa kulikonse, kulipidwa pomwepo popanda ma chargeback, ndi kufikira ogwiritsa ntchito Bitcoin padziko lonse — zonse popanda mapangano kapena ndalama za mwezi.

entries.englishValue: Bitcoin isn't just useful at the cash register — it's a better form of money that protects your savings, your privacy, and your freedom to transact. Here's a quick overview.
entries.targetTranslation: Bitcoin sili yothandiza chabe pa kasha — ndi mtundu wabwino wa ndalama yomwe imateteza zomwe mwasunga, chinsinsi chanu, ndi ufulu wanu wochita malonda. Apa pali baibulo lalifupi.

entries.englishValue: You just scanned a Bitcoin Accepted Here sticker. Here's why that's great news — for this business, and for you.
entries.targetTranslation: Mwangosanthula chitikiti cha 'Bitcoin Imalandiridwa Pano'. Apa ndi chifukwa chake izi ndi nkhani yabwino — kwa bizinesi iyi, ndi kwa inu.

entries.englishValue: The business you're at accepts Bitcoin — a modern, open-source payment network that anyone can use, anywhere in the world, without banks or middlemen taking a cut.
entries.targetTranslation: Bizinesi yomwe muli nayoyi imalandira Bitcoin — netiweki ya malipiro yamakono, yotseguka yomwe aliyense angagwiritse ntchito, kulikonse padziko lapansi, popanda mabanki kapena apakati otenga gawo.

entries.englishValue: Below is the short version of why accepting Bitcoin is good for this business, plus why using Bitcoin is good for you as a customer.
entries.targetTranslation: Pansipa pali baibulo lalifupi la chifukwa chake kulandira Bitcoin ndi kwabwino kwa bizinesi iyi, ndi chifukwa chake kugwiritsa ntchito Bitcoin ndi kwabwino kwa inu monga kasitomala.

entries.englishValue: Nostr clients are free apps that let you read and post on the Nostr network. All of them are interoperable — you can switch clients anytime and keep your followers and content.
entries.targetTranslation: Ma client a Nostr ndi mapulogalamu aulere omwe amakulolani kuwerenga ndi kulemba pa netiweki ya Nostr. Onse amalumikizana — mukhoza kusinthana motha pakati pawo popanda kutaya akaunti yanu.

entries.englishValue: Nostr is a new decentralized protocol for communicating online — no single company controls it, Bitcoin zaps are built in, and you can move between apps without losing your followers.
entries.targetTranslation: Nostr ndi protocol yatsopano yopanda wolamulira yolumikizirana pa intaneti — palibe kampani imodzi yomwe imayilamulira, ma zaps a Bitcoin amapangidwa mu netiweki.

entries.englishValue: What is Nostr?
entries.targetTranslation: Kodi Nostr ndi chiyani?

entries.englishValue: Nostr is similar to email: no one owns the protocol, anyone can build an app on top of it, and you can pick whichever app you like best. Unlike Twitter or Facebook, there's no central company that can censor, deplatform, or deboost you.
entries.targetTranslation: Nostr ikufanana ndi imelo: palibe amene ali ndi protocol, aliyense akhoza kupanga pulogalamu pamwamba pake, ndipo mukhoza kusankha pulogalamu yomwe ikukhutiritsani.

entries.englishValue: Nostr is a new protocol that lets you communicate online without fear of censorship, deplatforming, or deboosting.
entries.targetTranslation: Nostr ndi protocol yatsopano yomwe imakulolani kulumikizana pa intaneti popanda mantha a kuletsedwa, kuchotsedwa, kapena kuchepetsedwa.

entries.englishValue: Platforms like Twitter and Facebook are controlled by a single company, but no one controls the Nostr protocol.
entries.targetTranslation: Mapulatifomu monga Twitter ndi Facebook amalamuliridwa ndi kampani imodzi, koma palibe amene amalamulira protocol ya Nostr.

entries.englishValue: Freedom to move
entries.targetTranslation: Ufulu woyenda

entries.englishValue: Nostr is similar to email. No one controls the email protocol, and anyone can build a client (like Gmail, Hotmail, etc.) on top of it.
entries.targetTranslation: Nostr ikufanana ndi imelo. Palibe amene amalamulira protocol ya imelo, ndipo aliyense akhoza kupanga client (monga Gmail, Hotmail, ndi zina).

entries.englishValue: No one controls the Nostr protocol either, and anyone can build a client (like Damus, Amethyst, etc.) on top of it.
entries.targetTranslation: Palibe amene amalamulira protocol ya Nostr nayonso, ndipo aliyense akhoza kupanga client (monga Damus, Amethyst, ndi zina) pamwamba pake.

entries.englishValue: If you don't like how a certain client works, you can seamlessly move your Nostr account to another client without losing your followers or content.
entries.targetTranslation: Ngati simukukonda momwe client inayake imagwirira ntchito, mukhoza kusunthira akaunti yanu ya Nostr ku client ina mosalephera popanda kutaya zinthu zanu.

entries.englishValue: Bitcoin is built in
entries.targetTranslation: Bitcoin yapangidwa mkati

entries.englishValue: Bitcoin is built in natively to the Nostr protocol. If you see content you like, you can easily zap Bitcoin to someone as a thank you!
entries.targetTranslation: Bitcoin yapangidwa mwachilengedwe mu protocol ya Nostr. Mukawona zomwe mwakonda, mukhoza kutumiza Bitcoin (zap) kwa wina mosavuta.

entries.englishValue: On centralized platforms like Twitter and Facebook, the centralized company earns money from your content. But on open protocols like Nostr, you earn money from your content.
entries.targetTranslation: Pa mapulatifomu apakatikati monga Twitter ndi Facebook, kampani yapakatikati imapeza ndalama kuchokera ku zomwe mukulemba. Koma pa Nostr yotseguka, ndalama zimapita kwa inu mwachindunji.
